The software has all the major necessities for a small sized company to do their bookkeeping properly. These include the customers and sales section which allows you to add either customers or jobs as sources of revenue depending on how your company operates. Quotes and proposals, sales orders, invoices, and time and expense tickets can all be created to track a companys sales data. There is also a free Mobil app available to sage users which allows all of the companys sales data and customers to be accessed at any time. The app is not interactive but the data can be viewed.  The Sage program also offers merchant services that allows credit card payments to be entered and processed directly in Sage. All the vendors and purchases of a company are tracked. Those, like the accounts receivable features, include tracking everything necessary for product or services companies. All of the inventories for the company can be tracked and purchase orders created. All employee information can be managed through Sage. The payroll services, however, do cost extra per year but that is the case for most accounting software like Sage. Lastly, all a companys banks and credit cards can be managed inside Sage.

Sage has more features, and overall I was very impressed with the software. The layout is very easy to comprehend. There are different tabs for each of the functions as I described before. Each of the tabs is laid out on the screen with all the individual steps necessary for proper bookkeeping. I think it helps to keep you organized and make sure nothing is missed. Also, once all of the individual steps are completed inside of the program you can pull basically any report you need with any of the information from all the departments.  Once you purchase the program there is also technical support available if you have any program needs, but after the first year it is not free.

Currently I use QuickBooks as an accounting program, and I would say they are both very similar. I do, though, think that Sage has a better layout to keep track of companies with more information.  It would probably be a good step up from the QuickBooks software for companies with more information. The only con to the Sage program is that, just like QuickBooks, there is no audit trail.

reviewText: I'm a big fan of Nancy Drew games, and The Secret of the Old Clock is a bit different from some of others.  This is the only Nancy Drew game that takes place in the past- in the 1930s.  It's also probably the easiest of the Nancy Drew games I've played.  Nancy undertakes to help her orphaned friend Emily, who has inherited her mother's inn, and fallen into a deep state of melancholy.  The inn has been experiencing strange accidents, and it's up to Nancy to figure them out.  The puzzles in this game were a bit easier than the standard Nancy Drew fare.  Also, there weren't as many locations to investigate as some other ND games.  In particular, there's very little to do in the inn, and one of the things ND games do so well is to set up spooky, old, searchable houses.  That said, the game is still fun, and this is a great ND game to start with, if one is new to the genre.

reviewText:
I uninstalled VideoStudio Ultimate X4 before installing VideoStudio Ultimate X6.  The first time I tried the X6 installation it failed.  I tried the install again and the second time it was successful.

Some of the new or improved features of VideoStudio Ultimate X6 are:
* Motion tracking (add text and images to moving objects)
* Use animations with transparent backgrounds
* Variable speed playback
* Ultra HD 4K (higher quality than 1080p)
* Custom motion paths (animate objects, titles, graphics, & video
clips)
* Auto-detect speech and add sub-titles
* Improved screen recording (a separate program)
* DSLR stop motion
* Enhanced Boris Graffiti 6 for title animation

The X6 interface looks quite like the X4 and X5 program screens and is also similar to other video editors.  The top left corner is the preview panel that displays your video; the top right corner is the library panel of files,  filters, and options; and the bottom is the timeline and tracks (there are 2 views:  storyboard and timeline).  There are 3 basic steps shown at the top along with the menu bar:  capture (import your files), edit, and share (export / burn DVD's).

In my opinion the import features are some of the worst I've seen. There is no File | Open command to open a single video file. You have to select a folder and then Videostudio is supposed to show you all of the videos in that folder--but apparently not the subfolders. Anyway, when I select my Windows video library folder, I get the message that "There is no valid content" even though that folder has 600 video files in various video formats--plus even more videos in subfolders. In the "2 Edit" screen, you can click on the Storyboard view icon and then drag and drop a video file there. However I was not able to drag and drop my avi files there. Bummer.

There are a number of easy options for exporting videos such as burning DVD & Blu-ray discs, exporting to Youtube and other online sites, exporting to tablets and cell phone file formats, etc.

I'm using Windows 7 64-bit and have an AMD quadcore 3.3 ghz CPU and didn't have any issues editing videos. Except at one point in time Videostudio stopped showing the pop-up notes when you move the mouse over an icon to find out the function of the icon. When I closed and restarted the program the pop-up notes came back.

When you start the program the Corel Guide comes up. If you click on the Learn tab there are 8 introductory videos to help you get started, especially with the new features.  For more info you can click on the Launch Help icon at the bottom of the Corel Guide screen.  Or you can download the Getting Started Guide and/or the User Guide.  You may find more help with the how-to videos posted on youtube. It's a very powerful program.  In some cases the learning curve for editing videos can be a bit steep. So far I haven't had any major problems with X6, but I'll post more as I've had a chance to edit more videos with X6.
summary: Improvements over VideoStudio X4.  Lots of features and options so the learning curve can be a bit steep sometimes

reviewText: 1) If you are considering this software, please be advised this is an old version, and they decided to cut the price on the newest release (currently priced at $32 with free Amazon shipping): Family Tree Maker Deluxe 2012 2) The 2011 and 2012 versions are different from previous incarnations of this software (the last version I had was from 2005 or 2006 I think). The new versions have way more features, but is also more complex/more convoluted. There is no way my grandfather would ever be able to understand or navigate this software. Also, you really need access to your own records, or online research, or a membership with Ancestry.com (free trial included) if you're going to actually fill out your family tree. This software will not do it for you. 3) If you've never undertaken a family genealogy before, you might want to consider starting out on Ancestry.com before buying any software. Granted, $30 for the 2012 version is a pretty cheap investment to get started, but anyone can get a 2-week or 30-day free trial on Ancestry (you don't need the software) and they have a free online tree-builder feature that is simple & straightforward. 4) If you want help building your family tree and internet research or software programs aren't your thing, please remember the LDS (Mormon) church offers free genealogical services to the public. If you just want to chart out your tree on old-fashioned graph paper, for example, you can accomplish this free via email, phone, or visiting a Mormon genealogy center. They will *not* try to convert you - these offices are very PR-friendly (though they may give your deceased family members one of their controversial posthumous baptism ceremonies). A central tenant of this denomination is knowing your family tree, so devotees can track down ancestors after the 2nd coming. They are therefore happy to help non-members in genealogical tasks. Over all, this is one of the simplest and most powerful video editing programs I've used.  It has incredible power and flexibility, especially at this price point.  Check it out.

I am absolutely astounded by how much this video editing software does, easily and quite intuitively.

As others have mentioned, it takes a long time to load, and each individual piece needs to be registered and activated, so your initial setup will take some time. But, for me, every step was smooth and trouble-free.

I've used several other brands of video editing software over the years, plus professional editing platforms (30+ years in television production), and was astounded by what the Cyberlink PowerDirector 11 Ultimate Suite does, and how easily it does it.

The tools available let you range from very novice up to near-broadcast pro levels, depending on how you use it and what you want to do. The video editing offered a wizard that prepped and packaged a video with cutesy effects all with a few clicks. For putting together a birthday video for grandma of the kids, without much effort or editing knowledge, this was super. There were effects and packages for a large variety of occasions and events.

Going into more manual video editing, I found the functions extremely easy to use without any laborious training or reading (print manuals were included, which I appreciated). It's drag-and-drop for most purposes--drag your video clips in in order, trim them, then drag in overlays, special effects, transitions, and titles. To alter something, like the titles, just double-click. It's really that easy. There's a ton of graphics and effects built in to use.

Stepping up to more advanced levels of use and editing capabilities, it's all there, too. Color adjustments, audio mixing and editing... all extremely impressive, yet quite easy to figure out how to use.

This beats every other piece of video editing software I've ever used. Very impressed.
